CB30: Adventure

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
From the start of Carte Blanche 30 years ago adventuring was always a big part of our stories. From 1996 when we flew to Katmandu, to interview the first South African Everest Expedition. Their team member Bruce Herrod had fell to his death and South Africans wanted answers.

From Sean Wisedale the first South African to conquer all Seven Summits to Eveline Tshabala. who despite her HIV positive status was - together with friends Zuki and Nomawethu preparing to climb all seven of the summits around the world.

We have captured extreme moments be it on land, sea or air and over the years we have met brave and intrepid men and woman who have pushed the boundaries of modern day adventure from Mike Horn and his Arctic adventure to Joey Evans who after recovering from a major bike accident finished the Dakar Rally. Riaan Mansers has had many extraordinary adventures - possibly the most frightening - was when he rowed with his then partner, now wife, Vasti, from Africa to the USA. Vasti became the only woman from the African continent to have rowed across any of the worlds oceans



Further information:
In May 2010, extreme athlete Lewis Pugh hiked up Mount Everest to Lake Pomeri situated just below the summit at 5 300 m….. it’s here, he broke all swimming records in 2 degree water. Five years down the line another group of extreme sportsman decided to challenge Lewis swimming record, a group of men who swim under the banner Madswimmer. Swimming in the freezing water in temperatures between 0.5 and 2 degrees in the highest known lake ever to have been swum in, Madswimmer achieved a new world record

We met free diver Michael Rutzen’s whose adventures in the deep with Sharks were beyond the pale. From Record break supersonic speeds to Soaring high above like a bird, are adventure and then there were adventures of the milder sort vintage car rally’s, steam trains.

Whilst South African students took part in Australia’s solar race from Darwin to Adelaide, 80 year old Julia Albu, travelled Africa in a 20 year old car.

Then from darkest Africa to the darkest hole, well cave actually. The deepest dry cave ever discovered in South Africa by a group of cavers. We went down with them…possibly the most frightening adventure we have taken part in.

Just a few of Carte Blanches adventures in our 30 years on air.

Script:


V/O 9 sec
1996, the first South African Everest expedition ended in controversy when team member, Bruce Herrod, fell to his death.

Derek: Some people have this image of you and Cathy on the summit of Everest with three sherpas and all the oxygen and Bruce Herrod on his own struggling many hours behind.
Ian: Everybody climbs Everest on their own…you go at your own speed from A to B.

V/O
Carte Blanche’s interview with expedition leader Ian Woodall in Khatmandu was a television first. Cathy O’Dowd, the first South African woman to summit this fabled mountain flew with us back to base camp.

Derek: It’s an incredible achievement…..Cathy congratulations.

Sean Wisedale: Seven Summits
Sean Do you remember that helicopter flight when I looked outside those windows at the Himalayas and that Helicopter’s flying the highest it can fly and mountains are 2 and a half kms higher than you, you know that something really special there.

V/O
Sean Wisedale the cameraman on the Everest shoot was so overwhelmed by the sheer magic of Everest he went on to become the first South African to climb all Seven Summits…

Sean: No 6

V/O
We joined him on Mt Kilimanjaro, his final summit.

Sean: We have all got our own mountains to climb but this Seven Summits journey has helped me to find mine.

V/O 13 sec
And in these past 30 years we’ve filmed the highs and lows, of adventurers intent on fulfilling their own awe inspiring dreams…..conquering the mountains within themselves

V/O 12 sec
Like Evelina Tshabalala who despite her HIV positive status was - together with friends Zuki and Nomawethu preparing to climb all seven of the summits..

Everest base camp dance

V/O
Carte Blanche’s hall of fame for explorers and adventurers is extraordinary.

Kingsley: Still carrying Livingstone’s body, Chuma and Susi would have crossed the Columbo River somewhere upstream from these falls

V/O
We have captured extreme moments be it on land, sea or air……

Link The time for talk is over 100’s of hours of flying experience are about to be compressed into a single minute of exacting aerobatics.

V/O 8 sec
Over the years we have met brave and intrepid men and woman who have pushed the boundaries of modern day adventure.

Mike Horn 2005
Mike One night I heard this…and I knew it was a polar bear coming closer//next minute I see the nose of the polar bear pushing through the tent about 25 cm from my head.

From Paraplegic to Dakar Finisher
And I have just come across a bike right here the rider has been evacuated he is obviously injured I am jus going to take everything off his bike that I need put it on to mine and just continue…fikking insane but it shows you you don’t quit ever…

Riaan Manser: Modern Day Adventure no safety net Take me 2 New York 2015

Derek: You say you don’t do back up boats and you don’t do an adventure unless there is a chance of dying?
Riaan: If we want to take modern day adventuring to a new level we can’t do things with a back up boat and then claim that reward.

V/O
Vasti became the only woman from the African continent to have rowed across any of the worlds oceans

Riaan This last journeys a love story its about somebody who is closest to you on the planet… I just wanted to stands up and tell Vast how proud I was of her and what she had done.

Derek: Extreme Athlete Lewis Gordon Pugh has braved water beyond cold, water few would even dare enter.

V/O
In May 2010 Lewis hiked up Mount Everest to Lake Pomeri situated just below the summit at 5 300 m….. it’s here he chose to take his record breaking dip in 2 degree water.

Lewis: Every time I took a stroke it’s a beautiful mountain Mt Everst it’s a very special place and it’s inspiring.

V/O
Derek So Lewis Pugh had set the bar at a height most polar bears would think twice about challenging and then five years down the line another group of extreme sportsman decided to have a go at it not surprisingly they decided to have a go at it.. not surprisingly they are called the Mad swimmers.

V/O 2015
From Laguna Verde in Northern Chile, the Madswimmers began their hike up the Andes It was a hard expedition, through stony terrain and vertical ice climbs.

Herman: You know first you climb a mountain for 7 hours… you see a frozen lake but to think you have got to swim there is not so cool…

Swimming in the freezing water in temperatures between 0.5 and 2 degrees in the highest known lake ever to have been swum in the Madswimmers achieved a new world record

Free diving with Sharks 2004
V/O
Free diver, Michael Rutzen’s mission is to change our perception of the Great White these misunderstood creatures of the deep.

Dubbed the Shark W for his extraordinary ability to interact with these supreme predators this SA has done what many believe to be impossible to free dive peacefully with great whites without a cage and without a weapon.
Michael: Free Diving is to me something wonderful, it’s an apex predator that allows you to interact with them.
John: And that’s not the image of Jaws …
Michael: That’s why we did it.

V/O
Extreme speed testing and breaking boundaries needs innovation on land or in the air…..

Richard Noble: Just picture this you are standing in the middle of the course and you see this car coming up faster than any jet fighter you have ever seen in complete silence and then you get the double bam….just like that.

V/O
Hakskeen Pan in the Northern Cape will be the site of this record breaking supersonic land speed record.

Richard …..The concept of the car is that it is a jet and rocket powered car, and principally the jet is there to do most of the hard work and the rocket is there as the booster.

V/O 9 and half sec Yves Rossey _ Jetman
Talking about rockets, we met up with Swiss pilot, Yves Rossey in Dubai. With carbon fibre wings of his own design, Yves was soaring

Up Sound: A helicopter land it’s pick up a man known as Jetman who has spent the last 20 years perfecting what to most of us s mission impossible
Jet man: To be able to fly…to have that freedom so close to the dream to be the bird.

Derek: Gentleman start your engines…….

V/O
On a somewhat slower note we took an adventure of a different sort.

The Riley rendezvous kicked off in Broederstroom……and Dulltroom..

V/O 2015
From vintage car expeditions around Africa to state of the art cars of the future.
The Solar challenge in Australia is where technology meets innovation; innovation meets adventure.
And for the first time 2 African teams were racing to the finish, the University of Kwa -Zulu Natal and the North West University.

Arnold: This is almost like the space programme but for Solar Cars, whatever we develop here a couple of years down the line it ends up in a car.
Link
When it comes to 5 in afternoon all teams stop exactly where they are and this is where they will start from the next morning.
Kirsty……….every second of sun that we miss is a second of driving we cant do the next day.

V/O 2017
For some turning 80, is the sunset of their lives for Julia Albu it meant nothing at all except for the start of the mother of all adventures.

Link
When you get an 80 year old, woman talking about driving all the way from the Cape to Cairo in a 20 year old car with more than 300 000 km on the the clock it may be difficult to take her seriously.
Julia “ You know I believe a car has a soul and she has been with me for 20 years.”

V/O
Julia drove off in June last year…. finally reaching her destination, Alexandria, Egypt in January.

Julia: I am besotted about the continent there is nothing to be afraid of there is only hospitality and warmth.

V/O 4 sec
From the Dark Continent to the Darkest Cave.

You just see this black space in front of you and as a caver that gets you really excited a massive passage came up again.
John: This cave is the deepest dry cave ever to have been discovered in South Africa…

V/O
Called Armageddon it is situated 45 minutes South West of Johannesburg.

Link: We are about 125 metres below surface `and it is inevitable you start seeing weird and wonderful formations….and this is one of the more weird and wonderful.
V/O
Here Arganite crystals line the cave walls.

Link: This is the infamous third pit at this point we are 225 metres below the surface at one time this was a caving record in South Africa.
Link: Well that is by far the most extraordinary thing I have ever done in my life, extraordinary and absolutely terrifying no wonder they call it Armageddon.
